title: Check if a value is a valid variable name
description:
Write a function `is_valid_variable_name(value)` that returns whether `value` is both a string and a syntactically valid Python identifier.

Unlike Day 4/18's identifier checks (which always receive a string), this one has to handle any type of input first - a non-string can't be a variable name at all.
hints: Idea to consider: check the type first, then the identifier rule
str.isidentifier() only exists on strings - calling it on a number would raise an AttributeError, so value's type needs checking before that method call is safe.
Guard with isinstance(value, str) before calling .isidentifier() on it, so a non-string input returns False instead of crashing.
expected_behavior: Returns True only if value is a string and a valid Python identifier.
explanation: isinstance() guards the isidentifier() call - without it, a non-string argument like 42 would crash the function instead of correctly answering 'no, that's not a valid variable name.'
